note:
Thirty-four measured regions resolve to 18 figure rows, 6 table rows and 10 exclusions, with nothing unaccounted. The exclusions are the display mathematics and the code: equations (1)-(4) on p9 are four pasted equation images, (7) and (8) on p11 are two more, (10) on p12 is a pasted body whose number alone stayed in the text layer, (11)-(13) on p12 are three pasted images inside one measured band, and the last two are the MATLAB code bands of pp25 and p27. The appendix lists its own source code page after page, and the same detector reads those monospaced bands as artwork.

What this paper adds to the lane. (1) It runs the figure numbers twice: the abstract's Figure 1 and Figure 2 are re-spent by the body's Figure 1 and Figure 2, and both pairs are real exhibits. (2) The abstract's two exhibits print in reverse order on the page - Figure 2 above Figure 1 - and the abstract's prose is set in two interleaved columns, so no lead sentence for either thumbnail survives as a contiguous string; the only readable lead for the surface is 'we analyze the possible superposition of waves, and get the three-dimensional simulation diagram of the waves, and simulate it'. (3) The same Excel chart is printed three times: as the abstract's Figure 2, as Figure 10, and as Figure 12 with a recast x axis - a duplicate-exhibit pattern no other paper in the batch has shown. (4) The caption side rule is the cleanest yet: side follows exhibit kind, figures below, tables above, 23 rows out of 23. (5) The caption numbering is the barest in the batch - 'Figure N' with no colon, no period, and a four-word title in the shortest case ('Table 1 Related Parameters').

Defects worth recording. p17 announces Table 2 as 'The following figure shows the atmospheric noise table' - the wrong exhibit noun. Table 4's caption prints 'f =15Hz' for a 15 MHz frequency. Table 1 prints 'w' for watts. Figure 4's decomposition tree labels the ionospheric term 'La' while equation (5) directly above it writes 'Li'. Figure 11's right frame is titled 'sea surface reflection loss' on a ground-reflection chart, because the plot was cloned from the sea case and one axis title was never edited. Figure 13's x ticks print '00' for the leading zero. Figure 12's x axis title sits below its own embedded data table, detached from the axis. Table 3's caption is a formula fragment with no verb. And every page carries a red Chinese shop-watermark band that on p19 and p25 crosses the running header.

What the record calls a pattern. The drawing pipeline is three tools and the census can name them: a MATLAB surf/plot export for every numeric exhibit, a pasted Excel screenshot for every chart that needed a printed table, and hand-drawn line art for every mechanism schematic. Grid style follows the tool too - native Word tables come out booktabs-like, imported multi-tier grids come out boxed with merged headers. That is the strongest tool-to-form coupling in the batch so far: in the earlier papers caption side followed either the exhibit kind or the part of the paper, here it follows the exhibit kind and the grid's rule style follows the software.

Section grammar. Section 4 is where everything is drawn: 13 of the 24 rows live between 4.1 and 4.3, one per modelling step, in the order loss mechanics (Figure 4), geometry (Figures 5-9), parameters (Table 1), and the first-reflection result (Figure 10). Section 5 re-runs the sea exhibits on ground (Figure 11, Table 3) and section 6 tabulates the multi-hop budget (Table 4, Figure 13) before recommending frequencies (Table 5). Every model step gets exactly one exhibit, and the two exhibits that are never announced by a sentence (Table 1, Table 4) are both parameter sheets rather than findings.
rules: The paper spends its figure numbers twice: the abstract prints 'Figure 1 The wave situation when the wind scale is 6' and 'Figure 2 The relationship between the wind scale and the first reflection intensity', and the body then opens section 4.1.2 with 'Figure 1 HF propagation diagram' and 'Figure 2 Inner layers of ionosphere' - four exhibits, two numbers, and no sentence anywhere reconciles the two runs [caption.numbering].

Numbering carries no punctuation at all: 18 figure captions print 'Figure N' and 5 table captions print 'Table N', a bare number followed by the title as a noun phrase, with no colon and no period in either set [caption.numbering].

Caption side is decided by exhibit kind and never varies - all 18 figure rows print their caption BELOW the artwork and all 5 numbered table rows print theirs ABOVE the grid - so the single page 16 that carries both kinds shows the rule twice in one column [caption.position].

Captions are titles, not descriptions: the eighteen numbered figure captions run 5 to 13 words with a median of 8, the table captions are shorter still (Table 1 four words, Table 3 five), and the longest title in the paper is the abstract's 13-word 'relationship between the wind scale and the first reflection intensity' [caption.words].

Only one caption names a plotted symbol, Figure 10's 'P1', and none names an axis quantity, a unit or a parameter value - so the caption names the exhibit's subject and the axis titles inside the image carry everything else [caption.variable_count].

No caption concludes anything and none states a direction of change: the reading sentence lives in the body text instead, and for the two Excel charts the reading sentence is the only place the trend is stated in words [caption.concludes].

Three-dimensional drawing appears in three exhibits across six measured rows - the abstract's surface, the four frames of Figure 3 and Figure 13 - and it is always the same MATLAB surf export, so the paper's 3-D is a surface-height aesthetic, not a scatter of points in space [geometry.three_d].

Exactly one exhibit carries a colour scale: Figure 13's jet colourbar, which encodes SNR from -50 to 100. Every other coloured surface in the paper is coloured by height with no scale printed, so the reader of Figure 3 cannot recover a value from a colour [geometry.colorbar].

Key placement never leaves the frame: 6 of the 18 figure rows carry a key and every one of them is inside, always at the upper right for a single frame and at the lower left for a two-frame pair, while the three pasted Excel charts key as a chip row floating inside the plot area and the twelve remaining rows - surfaces and schematics - carry no key at all [geometry.legend].

Panel count follows the comparison being made: 14 rows stand on a single frame and the 4 two-frame rows are all side-by-side pairs - night vs day, two polarisations, two grazing angles, sea vs ground - while Figure 3's four frames are measured as four separate rows because the export left a wide gutter between them, which makes the paper's only 2x2 the one place where panel_count and doc_order disagree [geometry.panel_count].

Shared axes are used in exactly half the pairs and only where the two frames plot the same variable on the same range: Figure 2's ionospheric bands share one Height(km) scale and Figure 5's frames share the 0-90 incident angle, while Figures 8 and 11 keep two independent y ranges inside one shared x axis - which is the reason Figure 8's y goes 0.97 to 1 in one frame and 0.84 to 1 in the other without any warning beyond the tick labels [geometry.shared_axes].

Family follows the drawing tool: the six surface exhibits are all MATLAB surf exports, the four line rows are MATLAB plot exports, the three bar rows are pasted Excel screenshots with their data tables burned in, and the five schematics are the paper's only line-artwork [geometry.family].

Rule style splits by the software that made the grid, not by the data: the four native Word tables keep booktabs horizontals with internal verticals and no outer box, the two imported multi-tier grids are fully boxed with a rule at every cell boundary, and no grid in the paper uses verticals alone [table.rule_style].
Shading happens once, in the uncaptioned notation glossary, and never in a captioned table - every grid that the paper numbers is flat white [table.zebra].
Merged header cells and a slanted corner appear only in Table 2, the one grid with three header tiers, so header complexity and the diagonal coincide in a single exhibit [table.diagonal_header].

Units sit in three different places under one roof: in the header parenthetically where the grid has a typed header row (Table 3's ε(F/m), Table 4's r(km)), in a dedicated Unit column where it has a header but no room for the unit (Table 1), and inside the stub cell where there is no header at all (Table 5's '2-4 MHz'), so 'where the unit goes' tracks the grid's shape rather than the table's subject [table.units_in_header].

No grid in the paper merges a body cell, continues across a page break, or prints a note row except the uncaptioned glossary, whose note line is the only sentence any grid prints under its rule [table.note_sentence].

Announcement is always same-page: all 21 rows that carry a mention have lead_pages 0, so the paper never names an exhibit on an earlier page than the one it prints on, and the uncaptioned notation glossary is the only row with no mention at all [mention.lead_pages].

Citations are deixis, not analysis: 21 of the 24 rows are reached by their own printed number, but the leaning sentence almost never repeats it - the habitual form is 'as follows:', 'we get the following chart by calculation:', 'The related parameters are shown in the table.' - and only Figures 7, 12 and 13 get a trail sentence that reads the exhibit back to the reader [mention.style].

Two exhibits are announced with the wrong kind word or with no number at all: p17 opens Table 2 with 'The following figure shows the atmospheric noise table' - the paper's only reader-lead that says 'figure' for a grid - and p18 introduces Table 3 as 'the table' with no number, so Table 3 is identified only by its caption [mention.lead_sentence].

Placement follows the argument rather than the page: 12 of the 24 rows sit in the middle band of their page, 8 in the top third and 4 at the foot, and the foot cases are all figures whose caption closes the page just before the next section heading opens the next [place.page_zone].

Exhibit density tracks the derivation: the abstract carries 2 rows, the model sections (4.1-4.4) carry 13, the result sections carry 5, the ground comparison 3, the notation glossary 1, and the appendix carries only code - which is excluded, not counted as artwork [place.section_kind].

Other symbols instruction will be given in the text.' Sixteen body rows in two columns, top rule and header rule and bottom rule with one internal vertical between the columns, and alternating grey row shading - the paper's only zebra banding anywhere.
